A symphony of sound, a dance of the tide;
The sand, a canvas, waiting to be told,
A story of the sea, in patterns bold.

The waves swept up, a swirling vortex,
A whirlpool of water, a maelstrom of might;
The sand, a treasure trove, of shells and of stones,
A hidden world, revealed in the ocean's throne.

When the tide pulled back, a poem was born,
A lyrical language, of waves and of form;
The patterns, a message, of the sea's own voice,
A call to the soul, a whispered, oceanic choice.

The poem read: "I am the ebb and the flow,
A constant change, yet a rhythm to know;
I am the waves, that crash and that roar,
A symphony of sound, forever in store."

A mystery, a wonder, a work of art;
It spoke of the tides, that rise and that fall,
A dance of the moon, a call to one and all.

A world of wonder, where creatures reside;
I am the waves, that crash and that play,
A symphony of sound, every single day."
